title: Temporary Patient Record Form
transcript:
Speaker 1: Good morning. How can I help you?
Speaker 2: Yes. I'm a visitor to this area. I had a sporting accident a little while ago, and I'm still in some pain. And I wondered if I could see a doctor here.
Speaker 1: Certainly, sir. We can take you on as a temporary patient. I'll just take down some personal details. Can I start with your name?
Speaker 2: Yes. It's Peter. Peter Smith.
Speaker 1: Right, Peter. And where are you staying here?
Speaker 2: At 95 Cross Street.
Speaker 1: And the suburb?
Speaker 2: Walkley. That's W A L K L E Y. Mhmm.
Speaker 1: And can I have a contact phone number?
Speaker 2: It's 46895324.
Speaker 1: Thanks. Okay. If you just wait down there, the doctor will see you in a minute.
Speaker 3: Now what can I do for you? It's Peter Smith, isn't it?
Speaker 2: Yes. I had a sporting accident and was treated by a doctor at home, but I'm still in pain.
Speaker 3: Right. I just need to ask you a few questions, first of all. Fine. Now what sport were you doing?
Speaker 2: I was playing tennis.
Speaker 3: Mhmm. I see. And what was the nature of your injury? Did you hurt your elbow or wrist?
Speaker 2: No. I had a sprained knee. That was the original problem.
Speaker 3: Right. And when did this happen?
Speaker 2: It was three weeks ago now. So that was June 18.
Speaker 3: Mhmm. Fine. And you say you had medical treatment?
Speaker 2: Yes. The doctor said I didn't need an X-ray or anything, and he just told me to use an ice pack.
Speaker 3: An ice pack.
Speaker 2: Fine. Yes. And I've been using a walking stick to help me get around.
Speaker 3: Right. Now what problems are you experiencing at the moment? Are you having any problems walking?
Speaker 2: Well, I can walk okay, but I still can't go upstairs, so I've been sleeping downstairs.
Speaker 3: Now you say your knee still hurts?
Speaker 2: Well, no. Actually, it's recovering nicely. It's my back that's hurting me now. It really aches at night and I can hardly sleep.
Speaker 3: Well, there's a few different things I can suggest for that. Great. First, you should put your stick away as that's probably the source of the problem. It'll be making you unbalanced.
Speaker 2: Oh, really? I wish I'd known.
Speaker 3: After that, I can prescribe you something to relax the muscles in your back.
Speaker 2: Oh, sorry to be difficult, but I've had something like that in the past and there were lots of side effects and I had to stop taking it. Can you recommend anything else?
Speaker 3: Well, yes. We do have a leaflet showing some exercises you can do to help yourself at home. If you do them every day, they'll soon be effective. Great. I'll do that.
